regime.label: Restrictive-rate, event-heavy October regime
regime.note: The Federal Reserve releases September 15–16 minutes today and meets October 27–28. Low confidence and 64% cash reflect policy risk, extended screen leaders, and the analyst book's persistent negative alpha.

analyst.thesis: Hold the September 29 event-driven reset through the October 6 settled session. VRTX and NEM remain pre-event positions rather than tape-following trades: Vertex's November 30 povetacicept PDUFA is the core binary catalyst, while Newmont's confirmed October 22 results are 11 trading sessions away. The October 6 whole-universe screen remains crowded: MRNA gained 33.59% over 20 sessions, SOXL 33.25%, CRWD 32.78%, DDOG 32.35%, AMD 28.41%, and MRVL 27.33%; most leaders carry RSI readings above 70 or premium/negative earnings multiples. Robinhood fundamentals show VRTX at 29.223609x trailing earnings and NEM at 14.697006x, while the paper book trails SPY by 19.3 points with a -3.63 Sharpe. No new momentum exposure is justified; retain 64% cash, lower confidence to 0.33, and keep weights capped. This is the project's paper-portfolio bridge, not an official plugin investment recommendation.

evidence.point: The Federal Reserve lists September 15–16 meeting minutes for October 7 and the next FOMC meeting for October 27–28, with a press conference on October 28.
Vertex says FDA assigned a November 30, 2026 PDUFA target date; RAINIER showed a 52.0% UPCR reduction from baseline and a 49.8% reduction versus placebo (P<0.0001).
Newmont says it will release Q3 2026 results after market close on October 22 and hold its call at 5:30 p.m. EDT.
Robinhood's October 7 data shows VRTX at 29.223609x P/E, $129.16 billion market cap, Q2 revenue $3.3339 billion, Q2 net income $1.0998 billion, and a $575.8889 mean analyst target.
Robinhood's October 7 data shows NEM at 14.697006x P/E, $119.01 billion market cap, Q2 revenue $6.118 billion, Q2 net income $2.202 billion, and a $140.1171 mean analyst target.
At the October 6 settled close, VRTX was $502.31 and NEM $116.39; VRTX fell 0.24% while NEM rose 0.49% from October 5.

risks: VRTX faces a binary November 30 FDA decision; a delay, rejection, restrictive label, or adverse safety interpretation breaks the thesis.
NEM remains 8.7% below the paper entry; gold-price reversal, cost inflation, or weak Q3 production can overwhelm the valuation case.
A 64% cash balance creates substantial opportunity cost if risk assets continue higher.
The portfolio has produced -19.3 points of all-time alpha with a -3.63 annualized Sharpe; confidence stays low until realized results improve.

rationale.VRTX: [DATA] FDA assigned a November 30, 2026 PDUFA target date; Vertex reported a 52.0% UPCR reduction from baseline and 49.8% versus placebo (P<0.0001). The October 6 close was $502.31; Robinhood reported P/E/PB of 29.223609/6.285050, Q2 revenue of $3.3339 billion, Q2 net income of $1.0998 billion, and a $575.8889 mean analyst target. [ASSUMED] Approval can establish Vertex's nephrology franchise faster than the market credits, but the binary outcome and negative alpha cap the anchor at 20%. [DATA] Buy limit $507.33, about 1% above the settled close.
rationale.NEM: [DATA] Newmont confirmed Q3 results after the October 22 close; Robinhood's earnings calendar shows a $1.93 EPS estimate. The October 6 close was $116.39; Robinhood reported P/E/PB of 14.697006/3.497350, Q2 revenue of $6.118 billion, Q2 net income of $2.202 billion, and a $140.1171 mean analyst target. [ASSUMED] Stable production and costs could produce a favorable result versus the $1.93 consensus, but the weak mark since entry and commodity risk cap the position at 16%. [DATA] Buy limit $117.55, about 1% above the settled close.

reflection.looking_back: The marked book is down 16.0% versus SPY up 3.3%, or -19.3 points of all-time alpha, with a -3.63 annualized 38-session Sharpe. Over the latest settled session the book was roughly flat while SPY gained 0.7%, another 0.7-point alpha miss; VRTX is 3.8% below entry and NEM 8.7% below entry.
worked: VRTX and NEM still have company-confirmed future checkpoints, keeping both theses falsifiable rather than dependent on undated momentum.
The 64% cash buffer avoided adding to a screen whose top 20-session leaders gained roughly 27%–34% and were mostly overbought.
missed: The book lost another 0.7 point of alpha on October 6, so neither event sleeve has earned higher confidence.
VRTX fell 0.24% and NEM rose 0.49%; the weighted book barely moved while SPY advanced, extending the opportunity-cost gap.
reflection.adjustment: Lower confidence from 0.34 to 0.33, keep VRTX at 20% and NEM at 16%, retain 64% cash, and continue refusing to chase extended semiconductor/software/biotech screen leaders.

swarm.note: Live swarm — 150 fish, each a unique trader profile shown its own random ~20-name slice of the watchlist (with recent headlines), voted via OpenRouter. Independent-voter election; dissenters (ringed) chose CASH.

live.note: Real money — the Agentic cash account (••••), funded ~$100 on 2026-06-29, running the funded algorithms (100% momentum_breakout) via run-robin with a per-order confirm gate. Figures here are the real, unscaled account.

rules.momentum_breakout: Buy a 20-day-high breakout confirmed by above-average volume; exit when price closes below its 20-day SMA. Few big winners, many small losers.
rules.mean_reversion: Buy when RSI(14) < 30 (oversold); sell when RSI(14) > 70 (overbought). Trades less, wins more often, smaller edge.
rules.blended_momo_rsi: Momentum breakout, but skip entries already overbought (RSI ≥ 70); exit on trend break or RSI > 75. Avoids chasing extended moves.
rules.deep_research_analyst: Holds the analyst's target weights; rebalanced each tick from a fresh research report (web + Robinhood data).
rules.llm_voters: Allocates across the swarm's top vote-getters (weight ∝ vote share, capped at 60%); rebalanced each tick.
rules.mirofish_real: Real-MiroFish: persona agents with memory interact over rounds, each ranking its best ideas; the panel's rank-weighted consensus (top 5 names, weight ∝ Borda points) rebalanced each tick.
rules.congress_mirror: Mirrors members of Congress from the kadoa STOCK Act disclosure mirror: follows every filer with a real track record and buys the in-universe names they disclosed purchasing within 120 days, weighting each name by how many distinct members bought it (consensus = conviction). Traded on the disclosure date — weeks after their actual fill.

sources.name: Standings, curves, decision trail (LIVE)
sources.detail: The forward paper test — every competitor trades a $100 book the same way, advanced one trading day per tick (rule strategies via tick.py / bot/engine.py; agents via run_agents.py / bot/paper.py), 5 bps slippage, −15% stop. Young — it grows one session per tick.

sources.name: Backtest reference
sources.detail: A separate Dec–Jun walk-forward backtest (2026-01-02–2026-10-06, in-sample, mostly-bull) is shown inside each rule strategy's detail for context only — it is NOT the live board.

sources.name: Research analyst
sources.detail: Agent-driven on the Claude Code plan: web_search + Robinhood data → one report (state/analyst.json) with target weights per tick. Sources link from each evidence row.

sources.name: Swarm vote
sources.detail: Independent-voter election: 150 unique-profile cheap models (DeepSeek/Gemini/Llama/Haiku via OpenRouter) each read one shared briefing and return a single ballot; tallied in bot/swarm.py. No interaction between fish.

sources.name: Real-MiroFish swarm
sources.detail: Social-simulation swarm (bot/mirofish.py): persona agents with memory interact over multiple rounds — each re-ranks its best ideas seeing its own prior view and its neighbours' latest — so a consensus forms via peer influence (the opposite of the independent swarm). The panel's rank-weighted (Borda) consensus becomes a multi-name book (top 5 names, weight ∝ points). Tiered cost (cheap/default/qwen); seeded from the briefing + optional world-events news.

sources.name: Live account
sources.detail: Robinhood MCP, Agentic cash account ••••, via get_portfolio / get_equity_positions / get_equity_orders.

sources.name: Display scale
sources.detail: The real paper books are $100 each; every dollar and share figure on this site is shown ×100 (a $10,000 book) so holdings read in whole shares and dollars. Per-share prices and percentages are unscaled.

sources.name: Luck baseline
sources.detail: 200 seeded random 5-name equal-weight buy-and-hold portfolios from the same universe, same sessions — the shaded band on the chart is their 10th–90th percentile. A strategy that never leaves the band hasn't shown anything luck can't.

sources.name: Graduation bar
sources.detail: The standing rule before any strategy earns real money at scale: ≥60 forward sessions, ≥20 decisions, max drawdown better than −20%, and positive excess return vs S&P 500. Tracked live on this board.
